messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated KV cache page faults and continuous-batching latency spike observed in us-east-1 (gpu-pool-3). Error rate for streaming RPCs up ~18%, p95 latency x4. Auto-mitigation not triggered. Investigation requested. Incident page: https://redwood.incidents/1765123456 :rotating_light:

alex_kim: Ack, I'm on it. Noticed a sudden increase in KV cache size and a flood of unique keys in the telemetry. Correlating with a rollout around 02:12 UTC.

priya: I'm looking at the deploy history — there was a change to the batching prefixing logic and a default max_batch_size bump to 64 at 02:10. Might be related.

mateo: Paging/block manager logs show repeated "block allocation failed" messages and metadata GC not keeping up. Suspect block size miscalc when new keys have longer prefixes.

sofia: Quick customer impact check: internal alerts show impacted tenant list: [acme-inc-prod, betacorp-staging, travelly-prod]. Latency increases mainly on /v1/stream and embed endpoints hitting dedicated pools in us-east-1.

alex_kim: Mitigation hypothesis: the batching change is expanding the prefix space so KV cache entries balloon; block manager then fragments and metadata grows causing eviction thrash. We should throttle batching and apply an eviction config to avoid full-blowup.

priya: Agreed. Plan: 1) apply temp config to cap max_batch_size=16 and enable prefix-dedup=true 2) tune block-manager eviction to aggressive LRU threshold at 70% and reduce block_size from 8MB -> 2MB on affected hosts 3) perform rolling restart of block-manager to pick up eviction changes 4) monitor.

mateo: I'll prepare the config patch. Rolling patch snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: inference-runtime-config
data:
  batching.max_batch_size: "16"
  batching.prefix_dedup: "true"
  kv.block_size_mb: "2"
  kv.eviction_policy: "lru"
  kv.eviction_threshold_percent: "70"
```

sofia: Before we push, can we test locally on a single node? Mateo, can you apply to a canary host (gpu-3a) first?

mateo: Applying to canary now on gpu-3a. Command: `kubectl apply -f canary-runtime-config.yaml -n inference && kubectl rollout restart daemonset/block-manager -n inference --selector=pool=gpu-3a`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for inference-runtime-config on gpu-3a at 02:34 UTC.

alex_kim: Observing canary: cache growth stopped within 90s, page fault rates dropping, stream p95 back to ~1.3x baseline. Good sign. Mateo, proceed with region-wide rollout of config with a 2-min pause between hosts.

priya: I'm coordinating communications. CX/CS notified: @csm_lina, please prepare a short note to impacted customers explaining we saw transient latency due to keyspace growth and we have mitigations in place.

csm_lina: On it. Draft: "We detected an internal prefixing regression that increased cache churn, causing elevated response times for some requests. We applied a fix to throttle batching and to improve cache eviction which has reduced latency. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a postmortem." Want me to send now or wait for full rollback confirmation?

alex_kim: Wait 10 mins for rollout to complete across pool. If metrics stay stable, send the note with :white_check_mark:.

mateo: Rolling across remaining nodes in gpu-pool-3. Using command: `kubectl apply -f inference-runtime-config.yaml -n inference && kubectl rollout restart daemonset/block-manager -n inference --field-selector=spec.nodeSelector.pool=gpu-pool-3` — doing canary -> staggered 3 at a time.

incident-bot: monitor-bot: Alert suppressed for us-east-1 group while mitigation in progress.

priya: I'm updating the incident page and creating a brief status for support channels. Support runbook follows: - mark affected tenants in support UI - escalate any live tickets referencing slow streaming to oncall - run ``/metrics query "kv_cache_pages{region=\"us-east-1\"}"`` every 60s until stable.

alex_kim: After the rollout we still see some hosts with high resident metadata. I've pushed an immediate metadata-trim command to those hosts: `/usr/local/bin/block-manager trim-metadata --retain-days=1` — this reduces retained metadata and should free indexes without GC pauses.

mateo: Executed trim on 5 hosts. After trim, p95 back to ~1.05x baseline across the pool. Error rate trending down.

sofia: Customer notes: acme-inc-prod saw ~15% increased tail latency for ~18 minutes; no errors returned, just slower streaming. betacorp reported request timeouts in staging; they had retries configured and recovered. Travelly showed small spike but within SLO.

priya: Status update for internal channel: Mitigation applied (batch cap + prefix dedup + eviction tuning + metadata trim). Rolling restart completed at 03:12 UTC. Metrics stable for 25 minutes. Marking incident as "mitigated" and moving to monitoring phase.

alex_kim: Post-mitigation actions (assigning): - alex_kim: root cause analysis + postmortem draft - mateo: unit test and integration test to ensure batching prefix doesn't explode keyspace - priya: deploy pipeline gating to prevent batch_size bump without perf test - sofia: monitor and validate that metadata trim doesn't regress correctness - csm_lina: customer communications and followups

sofia: One more note: block_manager reported a small metadata leak in logs — `metadata_ref_count++ without release at block_id=...` I captured logs and opened GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/block-manager/issues/412. Worth pairing on root cause.

eng-oncall: Handoff: alex, I'm on for the 04:00-12:00 shift. Please add any outstanding tasks before you sign out.

alex_kim: Thanks — leaving the incident in monitoring. Outstanding: verify no regression in eu-west region (we saw a small bump earlier but not as bad). Postmortem draft targeted EOD. Tagging @sofia and @mateo for follow-up. :eyes:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status changed to MITIGATED by alex_kim at 03:20 UTC. Please continue monitoring; create a follow-up thread for the postmortem.

priya: Closing note: Customer message sent to impacted tenants at 03:28 UTC. Will include timeline and remediation steps in postmortem. :white_check_mark:

csm_lina: Thanks team. I'll loop in account reps for personal outreach where needed.

mateo: Leaving logs and patch diff in the incident page. Next steps: revert temporary config after we land the proper fix and controller-level guardrails.

alex_kim: Good work. If anything spikes again ping @eng-oncall and escalate immediately. Signing off for now. :white_check_mark:

eng-oncall: Acknowledged, taking over monitoring.
